concepts.title: Standard Form
concepts.ncert_text: A quadratic equation in variable x is an equation of form ax^2 + bx + c = 0, where a, b, c are real numbers and a ≠ 0.

concepts.title: Roots by Factorisation
concepts.ncert_text: Finding roots by splitting the middle term. If we can factorise ax^2 + bx + c = 0 into two linear factors, the roots can be found by setting each factor to zero.

concepts.title: Quadratic Formula
concepts.ncert_text: The roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0 are given by x = [-b ± √(b^2 - 4ac)] / 2a, provided b^2 - 4ac ≥ 0.

concepts.title: Nature of Roots
concepts.ncert_text: Depends on discriminant D = b^2 - 4ac. (i) D > 0: Two distinct real roots. (ii) D = 0: Two equal real roots. (iii) D < 0: No real roots.
